name: Play background location policy
plain: Apps that read location while closed must justify it to Google with a video and form.
meaning: Background location is the most sensitive mobile signal. Play requires a feature that needs it, a prominent disclosure, and approval. iOS shows 'Always Allow' reminders instead.

android.prompt_ui: Separate prompt since 11; Settings route only
android.store_policy: Play: declaration form with video; core functionality; deadline in 2021

ios.prompt_ui: While Using, then Always upgrade; periodic reminders
ios.note: iOS 13 added Allow Once and delayed Always prompts.

limits.headline: Can follow your location while closed, only if Google approves and you pick Always
limits.user_action: You tap Always allow, or change it in Settings after a first While using choice
can: Follow your location in the background for features like trip tracking, after approval
Ask for the Always choice after you first allow While using (iPhone)
Remind you now and then that it is using your place (iPhone)
cannot: Be approved on Google Play without a video, form and a feature that needs it
Ask for always access in the first Android prompt; Android 11 and later sends you to Settings
Keep Always access hidden from you
limits.differs: Android needs a Settings route and a Play approval. iPhone adds Allow Once and delayed Always prompts.

story.what_it_is: Google's rule that apps must prove a good reason before tracking you while closed.

marketing.name: Background location access
marketing.pitch: Apps must show a feature that needs it, and tell you clearly, before reading location in the background.

marketing.name: Always Allow reminders
marketing.pitch: iOS shows periodic reminders when an app uses your location in the background.

story.for_you: You see a prominent explanation, then a separate step to choose 'Allow all the time'. Later the phone may remind you which apps use your location in the background.
story.for_makers: Background location is the most sensitive signal on a phone, so Play asks for a video and form before approval. Real needs like geofenced reminders and family sharing pass; ad data collectors do not.

use_cases.example: A navigation app keeps guiding you when you lock the screen, so it needs location in the background.
A running tracker records your route while the screen is off and the phone is in your pocket.
A family app shows where your kids are on a map and alerts you when they reach school.
A walking game counts steps and finds creatures as you move around town with the app closed.
A courier app updates your order's live position even if the driver switches to a call.
A lost phone finder keeps reporting position so you can get it back.
An ad data SDK was caught selling background location to data brokers, which is why the rule exists.

story.android_note: Android 10 and 11 added a separate 'all the time' step, and Play requires approval.
story.ios_note: iOS offers 'Allow While Using' first and shows later reminders about background use.
